aspect: The code exists, and the label does not agree with itself
description: ISO 3166 assigns PS and PSE, listed as 'PS PALESTINE, STATE OF'. Older systems still carry 'PS Palestinian Territory, Occupied'. Depending on the implementation the entry files under P for Palestinian Territory, O for Occupied, or S for State of Palestine - so scanning a dropdown alphabetically frequently fails even where the entry is present.
energy_note: It's in the list. Under a letter you wouldn't think to check.

aspect: The document says a word that is not in the dropdown
description: Since 16 June 2023 the PA biometric passport's nationality field reads PALESTINIAN. The dropdown, where it exists, says 'Palestine' or 'Palestinian Territory'. The word on the document does not match the option on the form, and the traveller has to guess which mismatch is safer.
energy_note: The passport and the form disagree about what you are.

aspect: Some systems use codes that other systems reject outright
description: Some immigration authorities record nationality with three-letter codes that may be PSE, XXP, or other X-variants - the ICAO codes for unspecified or undefined nationality and for stateless persons. Booking systems that validate only against ISO 3166 reject those codes.

aspect: There is no home airline whose system is guaranteed to cope
description: Palestine has no operating national carrier, so there is no airline whose systems are built to handle these codes as routine, and foreign carriers' support agents are generally unfamiliar with the issue.
energy_note: No airline for whom you are a normal customer.

aspect: The mismatch surfaces later, at the worst point
description: Airline departure control transmits the MRZ code to border systems. A dropdown selection that differs from the MRZ can pass at booking and fail at check-in or at the border, by which time the flight is non-refundable.
energy_note: Fine at booking. Wrong at the gate.

aspect: SCENARIO - the form with no answer
description: The visa portal requires country of birth. Her options are Israel, Jordan, and a blank. Her birth certificate says Gaza. She picks one, knowing that whichever she picks is a discrepancy against one of her other documents, and that the discrepancy is what they will ask about.
energy_note: Three options, none of them true.

aspect: The administrative erasure is felt as the political one
description: Being absent from a dropdown is trivial and is not experienced as trivial. It is the daily, mechanical form of the argument about whether the place exists, delivered by a web form, several times a year.
energy_note: Your country, not found, please select another.
